name: US Fourth of July heat dome
headline: Ridge drew humid Gulf air; lasted over a week.

sections.The setup: Pronounced upper ridge over the eastern US.
sections.The trigger: Ridge drew humid Gulf air; lasted over a week.
sections.What amplified it: Heat index forecast at 105–115 °F (NWS forecasts, not observations); record 5-day heat stress.
sections.Climate signal: WWA ('Fossil fuels are heating America's 250th birthday', July 2026, Table 2) estimates that human-induced warming made the peak 5-day humid heat stress (WBGT) of this event in the eastern United States and Canada about 1.5 °C higher (95% interval about 0.3 to 2.2 °C; other analyses 0.5 to 0.8 °C) than in a pre-industrial climate: an attributable change in the event's peak 5-day wet-bulb globe temperature, not a global temperature anomaly and not a departure from the local normal.
sections.Still open: Summary entry: the full deep-dive (day-by-day timeline, steering, how it ended, sources) has not been written yet. It will be added as the log works back through the year.
